sections.html:
Etowah County is in northeast Alabama, with Gadsden as the seat and the largest city, and it makes up the Gadsden metro area. The 2020 census counted 103,436 residents and the 2025 estimate is 103,886, so the county has hovered near 100,000 people for decades. Households numbered 41,974 in 47,306 housing units, and 11.3 percent of the units were vacant. Owners occupy 71.1 percent of occupied homes and renters 28.9 percent. The homeowner vacancy rate is 1.7 percent and the rental vacancy rate is 10.1 percent. Urban areas hold 56.8 percent of residents and rural areas 43.2 percent. The median age is 42.4.

Stable numbers mean buyers are mostly people who already live nearby, and a rental vacancy rate above 10 percent means a rental house may sit a while. About 19.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, so exemptions for older owners come up often.

The seven cities are Attalla, Boaz (partly in Marshall County), Gadsden, Glencoe (partly in Calhoun County), Hokes Bluff, Rainbow City and Southside (partly in Calhoun County). The towns are Altoona, Reece City, Ridgeville, Sardis City and Walnut Grove. Alabama City is a former city, so older records may use that name, and a very old record from the 1860s may carry the Baine County name, since the county was first created under that name.

Four districts serve the county: Attalla City, Boaz City, Gadsden City and Etowah County Schools, which covers everything outside the limits of Attalla, Boaz and Gadsden. A house on the line between a city and the county system should be checked against the district map before a listing claims a school.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent on January 1. The county posts the full calendar, and an unpaid account follows it to a sale.

  • October 1: tax due
  • January 1: tax delinquent
  • February: turned over to Probate Court
  • March: Probate Court meets
  • April: advertised for sale
  • May: tax sale

The Revenue Commissioner is not required to mail tax notices and does so as a courtesy, so a missing statement does not excuse a late payment. You can pay by mail, in person at the county tax office, or through a mortgage company.

Interest and penalty run at 12 percent a year on past due taxes, and property is sold yearly for unpaid taxes. An owner has 3 years from the sale to redeem by paying the taxes, interest, fees and penalties at the same 12 percent rate.

A person who pays someone else's taxes gains no ownership by doing so. A buyer of a house inherits any unpaid prior years, because taxes follow the property. That is why a title opinion comes before any purchase.

Questions about appraised value go to the Revenue Commissioner, whose office is in the County Courthouse. The regular homestead exemption can be claimed on a principal residence regardless of age or income. It exempts $4,000 of assessed value for state tax and $2,000 for county tax.

TypeWho qualifiesWhat is exempt
Homestead IIOver 65, blind or totally disabled, taxable income of $7,500 to $12,000State tax and $5,000 of county tax
Homestead IIISame group, taxable income below $7,500All property tax
Homestead IVSame group, income above $12,000County tax up to $2,000

Exemptions must be applied for between October 1 and the third Monday in January, but regular homesteads can be claimed all year. Types II, III and IV need a yearly signed filing with tax returns. Nothing is automatic, so the exemption has to be claimed with the Revenue Commissioner.

Alabama sets four classes. Utilities are assessed at 30 percent, all other property at 20 percent, farm, forest and owner-occupied property at 10 percent, and motor vehicles at 15 percent. An owner-occupant therefore pays on a smaller share of value than a landlord does, which matters if a buyer plans to rent the house out.

sections.h2: Buying and selling at the courthouse
sections.html:
After a sale, the buyer records the deed in the Probate Office and then assesses the property at the Revenue Commissioner's office, bringing the deed along. Buyers should get a title opinion first, because delinquent taxes follow the property. The recording privilege tax is fifty cents per $500 of value under Alabama Code 40-22-1, plus the recording fee.

As the seller, you can save your buyer time by clearing the tax record first.

  1. Ask the Revenue Commissioner for a payoff on every year owed.
  2. If you hold a homestead exemption, tell the office the house is being sold.
  3. Keep invoices and permits for any storm repairs. An F4 tornado struck the county on Palm Sunday, March 27, 1994, so buyers of older houses ask.
  4. Let the title company confirm the payoff in writing.

We buy Etowah County houses as they stand, including ones with unpaid tax. The balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, and a cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the repair requests that follow an inspection.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell in Gadsden and the surrounding towns
sections.html:
Start with the basics a buyer will check. Is the deed in your name, or in the name of someone who has died? Are the tax years paid? Does the house sit in a city, in the county system or on the line between two districts? Answers to those three questions shape almost everything that follows. A short call to the courthouse often settles them in a single morning.

If you rent the house, think about how that affects a sale. A tenant in place may stay or may leave, and a buyer who wants the house empty will price in the wait. A vacant rental carries a full tax bill with nothing coming in, which is why many owners decide to sell rather than hold. Rental vacancy in the county is above 10 percent, so a long wait for a new tenant is realistic.

A conventional sale usually runs through a lender. The lender orders an appraisal, the buyer's inspector writes a repair list and a closing date slips while each step finishes. With a cash buyer there is no loan to approve. You still have the title search, the tax payoff and the deed recording, and those are the items to start early.

The offer reflects the house as it is, so you do not paint, patch or haul away old furniture. If there is a lien or an unpaid year of tax, the title company subtracts it at closing and you see the number on the settlement statement before signing. Compare that with the cost and time of preparing the house for a retail listing, and decide which route suits you.

Gather these before the first call: the deed, the latest tax statement, any notice from the county and a note on who lives in the house now. With those in hand, a conversation about price and timing takes minutes.

sections.h2: If a tax sale is near
sections.html:
The calendar above moves quickly once January arrives. If your house is delinquent and you are weighing a sale, the months between February and May are the tightest. Ask the Revenue Commissioner exactly where your account stands. If the property has already been sold for tax, the 3-year redemption period gives you room, though interest and penalties keep growing at 12 percent a year, so waiting costs money.

An owner in that position can still sell. The title company has to clear the tax sale and the redemption amount from the proceeds, and it will want the paperwork from the sale. Bring every notice you received, even the ones you set aside.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Etowah County, Alabama?
faqs.a: Gadsden, which is also the largest city. The Revenue Commissioner's office, where assessments are handled, is in the county courthouse.

faqs.q: When are Etowah County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, delinquent January 1, with a tax sale in May.

faqs.q: How much interest applies to late taxes in Etowah County?
faqs.a: Twelve percent a year on past due taxes.

faqs.q: Can I redeem a property sold for taxes in Etowah County?
faqs.a: Yes, within 3 years of the sale, by paying taxes, interest, fees and penalties at 12 percent a year.

faqs.q: Do I get the Etowah County homestead exemption automatically?
faqs.a: No. It has to be claimed with the Revenue Commissioner. The regular homestead can be claimed year round on a principal residence.
